unit_description: This unit shows equivalent fractions on number lines. Students identify fractions at the same number-line location, find equivalents using number lines, graph equivalent fractions, and connect models, number lines, and equations.
unit_goals: Identify fractions at the same number-line location.
Find equivalent fractions using number lines.
Connect models, number lines, and equations.
Understand why equivalent fractions occupy the same point.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students locate equivalent fractions at the same point on a number line and connect number lines to models and equations.

lessons.lesson_title: Fractions at the Same Number-Line Location
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by marking 1/2 and 2/4 on the same number line.
lessons.concept: Equivalent fractions are located at the exact same point on a number line. If two fractions are at the same place, they name the same amount and are equivalent.
lessons.practice: Identify fractions that share the same location on a number line.
lessons.objective: Identify fractions at the same number-line location.

questions.prompt: Are 1/2 and 2/4 at the same place on a number line?
Are 1/3 and 2/6 at the same place?
Are 2/3 and 3/4 at the same place?

learn.title: Fractions at the Same Number-Line Location
teaching_points: Equivalent fractions land on the same point.
Different names for the same point are equivalent.
Use the number line to check equivalence.

example.prompt: Mark 1/2 and 2/4 on a number line. Where do they land?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Which fraction is at the same point as 1/2: 2/6 or 4/8?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Tell which fraction is at the same location on the number line.

flashcards.title: Same Location on Number Lines
flashcards.instructions: Review same number-line locations for equivalent fractions.

bigIdea.title: Fractions at the Same Number-Line Location
bigIdea.subtitle: Same point, same amount
bigIdea.intro: When two fractions are at the exact same spot on a number line, they are equivalent. The number line is a powerful way to check if fractions are equal.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does a number line show that fractions are equivalent?

ruleCards.equation: same point on the number line
ruleCards.description: Fractions at the same distance from 0 are equivalent.
If the marks land on the same point, the fractions are equivalent.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by partitioning a number line into different numbers of equal parts and finding matching points.
lessons.concept: To find an equivalent fraction on a number line, partition the same 0-to-1 interval into more equal parts. The equivalent fraction will be at the same location.
lessons.practice: Use number lines to find fractions equivalent to a given fraction.
lessons.objective: Find equivalent fractions using number lines.

questions.prompt: Partition 0 to 1 into halves and fourths. What is 1/2 in fourths?
questions.hint: One half is the same as two fourths.

questions.prompt: Partition 0 to 1 into thirds and sixths. What is 2/3 in sixths?
questions.hint: Two thirds is the same as four sixths.

questions.prompt: Partition 0 to 1 into fourths and eighths. What is 3/4 in eighths?
questions.hint: Three fourths is the same as six eighths.

learn.title: Find Equivalents Using Number Lines
teaching_points: Start at the location of the given fraction.
Partition the 0-to-1 interval into more parts.
Find the new fraction name for the same point.

example.prompt: Find a fraction equivalent to 1/3 using a number line with sixths.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Find a fraction equivalent to 2/5 using a number line with tenths.
try_it.hint: 2/5 and 4/10 are at the same point.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find an equivalent fraction for each given fraction using the number line.

flashcards.title: Find Equivalents on Number Lines
flashcards.instructions: Review finding equivalents on number lines.

bigIdea.title: Find Equivalents Using Number Lines
bigIdea.subtitle: Partition into smaller parts
bigIdea.intro: You can find equivalent fractions by making smaller equal spaces on the same number line. The new fraction will point to the same place as the original.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does partitioning into more parts help find equivalent fractions?

ruleCards.description: Divide each equal part into 2 smaller equal parts.
The new fraction is at the same point as the old one.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by placing multiple fraction labels at the same point on a number line.
lessons.concept: Graphing a fraction on a number line means placing a point and writing its label. Equivalent fractions can share the same point with all their labels.
lessons.practice: Graph fractions on number lines and label equivalent fractions at the same point.
lessons.objective: Graph equivalent fractions on number lines.

questions.prompt: Graph and label 1/2 and 2/4 at the same point on a number line.
Graph 2/3 and 4/6 at the same point.
Graph 1/4 and 2/8 at the same point.

learn.title: Graph Equivalent Fractions
teaching_points: Place the point at the correct location.

example.prompt: Graph and label 1/2, 2/4, and 3/6 on a number line.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Graph 3/4 and 6/8 at the same point.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Graph and label each pair of equivalent fractions on a number line.

bigIdea.title: Graph Equivalent Fractions
bigIdea.subtitle: Put the labels on the same point
bigIdea.intro: When you graph equivalent fractions, they all go at the same point. You can write each fraction name above or below that point.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you graph two equivalent fractions on the same number line?

ruleCards.description: Partition the number line with enough parts for both fractions.
Write both fraction names at the same point.

lessons.lesson_title: Connect Models, Number Lines, and Equations
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing an area model and a number line for the same fraction.
lessons.concept: Fractions can be shown with area models, number lines, and equations. All three representations should match. 1/2 = 2/4 can be shown with a shaded model, points on a number line, and multiplication.
lessons.practice: Connect area models, number lines, and equations for equivalent fractions.
lessons.objective: Connect models, number lines, and equations for equivalent fractions.

questions.prompt: An area model shows 2/4 shaded. What is the equivalent fraction?
questions.hint: Half of the whole is shaded.

questions.prompt: A number line shows 3/6 and 1/2 at the same point. Write the equation.

learn.title: Connect Models, Number Lines, and Equations

example.prompt: Show that 1/2 = 3/6 using a model, number line, and equation.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Connect 2/4 = 1/2 using a model, number line, and equation.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Show each equivalent fraction pair with a model, a number line, and an equation.

flashcards.title: Connect Representations
flashcards.instructions: Review connecting models, number lines, and equations.

bigIdea.title: Connect Models, Number Lines, and Equations
bigIdea.subtitle: Three ways to show the same fraction
bigIdea.intro: Fractions can be shown with area models, number lines, and equations. Each representation gives a different view, but they all describe the same amount.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why are models, number lines, and equations useful for fractions?

ruleCards.description: Shows the amount of the whole that is shaded.
Shows that two fractions name the same amount.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of same location, finding equivalents, graphing, and connecting models/number lines/equations.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: fractions at the same number-line location, finding equivalents using number lines, graphing equivalent fractions, and connecting models, number lines, and equations.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.

warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Equivalent Fractions
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: fractions at the same number-line location, finding equivalent fractions using number lines, graphing equivalent fractions, and connecting models, number lines, and equations.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about equivalent fractions on number lines?

ruleCards.description: Equivalent fractions land at the same point on a number line.
Split each part into smaller equal parts to find equivalents.
